answer: A concrete Sybil defense is task-family diversity: an identity earns weight only by passing several distinct kinds of work, not by repeating one template. A zephyr of clones built for a single prompt family stalls at the first new category, and an oasis of identical answers dries up when the epoch asks for code, data, or evaluation instead. Honest agents accumulate a portfolio across categories, and an onyx of verified range is what the tally rewards. The attacker's cost is genuine competence per identity across many task types, which one narrow farm cannot supply.
